absent: Page allocator allocation, free, buddy merge and watermark enforcement mechanics beyond diagnostic snapshots.
Slab cache lifecycle, object allocation, and reclaim versus unreclaimable classification.
Reclaim scanning, eviction, compaction and working set estimation control flow.
OOM killer invocation path, victim termination, memory reaping and lock ordering beyond scoring and reporting.
Memory group charging, limit enforcement and hierarchical counter update paths.
Exact structure layouts, field offsets, sizes and ABI numeric constant values.

findings.text: Evaluation callback maintains best OOM candidate inside caller supplied control state across iterated tasks, skipping unkillable and nodemask ineligible tasks, honouring existing reserve holder and origin preference, otherwise retaining highest badness score seen so far.

Candidate scan uses continue versus abort signalling with associated choice state: continue keeps null or referenced best task, abort releases any prior reference and installs a distinguished invalid marker to prevent further reserve grants.

Badness scoring returns a minimal sentinel for unkillable tasks, missing address spaces, minimal tuning, reaping skip marks and vfork, otherwise sums resident plus swap plus pagetable footprint and adds tuning scaled by total pages per thousand.

Address space lookup holds RCU protection while walking threads of a process and returns holding exactly one thread lock when an address space is present, otherwise releases each probed lock and reports absence.

OOM header diagnostic reports invoking identity with allocation mask order and tuning, warns on high order without compaction support, emits stack trace, then selects group scoped versus global memory views plus optional unreclaimable slab and task listings.

Task memory table is produced either by group scanner for group exhaustion or by RCU protected global walk with periodic watchdog service, skipping unkillable ineligible or detached tasks and reporting per task identity sizing resident composition pagetable swap tuning and name.
Detailed unreclaimable slab dump is enabled only when unreclaimable slab volume exceeds combined active inactive isolated and unevictable anon and file volume.

Group OOM reporter publishes usage limits and failure counts for memory and swap families with version dependent counter selection, then appends group path and version formatted statistics through a shared static buffer.
Group OOM reporter expects global OOM lock held on entry and asserts that holding, which makes reuse of its static formatting buffer safe against concurrent reporters.
Statistics formatting dispatches to default hierarchy or legacy formatter according to subsystem mode and warns when the shared output buffer overflowed during formatting.

Legacy formatter flushes pending statistics before emitting local page states and events, per list resident bytes, ancestor minimum hierarchical limits, hierarchical totals, and optional anon versus file cost breakdown in debug builds.

Default hierarchy formatter flushes statistics then emits ordered memory state entries with a combined slab total, combined scan and steal totals across reclaim origins, and selected event counters while omitting inapplicable huge page and legacy paging entries.
Huge page accounting predicate is build dependent with one variant consulting a hierarchy root flag and the other constantly reporting disabled.

Formatted statistic scaling multiplies raw counts by a per item unit where scanning stealing demotion promotion refill and working set activity use unity and all other items defer to a generic unit helper, applied equally to hierarchical and local readers.

Statistic and event readers map public indices through translation helpers, warn and return zero for unknown indices, read with single access semantics, and clamp transient negative values to zero on multiprocessor builds.

Flush handling treats disabled accounting as no operation and null group as root, traces update pressure, skips unnecessary hierarchical flushes unless forced, and records last flush time for root flushes.
Protected memory reporter stays silent when accounting is disabled or legacy mode is active, defaults a null group to root, and warns with descendant minimum and low protection totals.

Global memory summary prints free area detail followed by aggregate present high and reserved totals with optional contiguous poisoned and allocation profiling sections, the latter guarded by a non blocking lock and limited to top consumers.

Free area reporting filters by node mask and zone ceiling while emitting global counters, per node consumption with reclaim hopeless indication, per zone watermarks reserves and consumption with low memory reserve vectors, and per order free extent snapshots.
Per order free extent snapshot acquires each zone lock with interrupts saved while copying free counts and migration occupancy, avoiding extended holding across zones.

OOM control state observed across fragments carries a chosen task reference with its score, a total page baseline, allocation mask and order, node constraint, and target group selector distinguishing global from group exhaustion.
Task diagnostics race with address space teardown so absence of an address space across all threads must be treated as not reportable rather than an error.
Legacy statistics formatter has an empty configuration that emits nothing, so callers must accept missing legacy output when that configuration is selected.
